## AI-writing check

**Overall:** This reads as human-written. No significant AI-writing tells turn up — no significance inflation, no AI-vocabulary words, no spaced em dashes or curly quotes, no formulaic contrast/rule-of-three pileups, and the piece is full of specific, checkable, idiosyncratic detail throughout.

### Findings
None. A pass through every category in the catalog — significance inflation, superficial-analysis tails, puffery, vague attribution, "challenges and future prospects" closers, AI-vocabulary density, copula avoidance, negative parallelisms, rule-of-three overuse, elegant variation, Title Case/boldface, inline-header lists, section summaries/disclaimers, em dashes, curly quotes/emoji, chatbot scaffolding — turned up nothing worth flagging. A couple of sentences use mild contrast constructions ("most of it is diagnosis, not wrenching"; "I didn't get a Slack message with a thumbs-up emoji. I got a guy in his seventies grinning...") that echo the shape of negative parallelism, but each pairs one concrete, specific image against another rather than knocking down a vague strawman, and together they form a single coherent thematic device — corporate abstraction versus tangible work — rather than a scattered verbal tic. Not worth flagging on their own.

### Reads as human
- Specific, checkable, unglamorous facts: Dave owned the shop for eleven years; Priya brings banana bread twice a month; Harold's Raleigh three-speed belonged to his father; Marcus needed his bike fixed in forty minutes; the shop is "wedged between a laundromat and a taqueria."
- Plain, blunt verbs and copulas throughout — "I quit," "I fixed bikes," "the frame was a mess," "his bottom bracket was shot" — with no *serves as / boasts / stands as* substitutes.
- Natural repetition instead of elegant variation: Dave, Harold, Marcus, and Priya are named and renamed plainly, never re-skinned as "the seasoned owner" or "the grateful customer."
- Sentence-case headings ("What the days actually looked like," "Two repairs I still think about," "Going back to an office") rather than Title Case.
- Hedges, asides, and a real point of view: "honestly there wasn't one dramatic moment," "which took some adjusting to," "that thought bothered me more than it should have," "That's probably the whole point."
- An unbalanced, escalating list — "a savings cushion, a growing suspicion that I'd forgotten what it felt like to finish something, and an ad on the shop's Instagram looking for part-time help that I'd been staring at for three weeks" — the kind of lopsided triad a person writes, not the flat three-adjective cadence AI defaults to.
- Straight quotes and apostrophes throughout, with no curly-quote mixing.

### Hidden characters
Clean — no invisible characters found. Ran `scripts/clean_text.py`, which reported no zero-width spaces, direction marks, word joiners, soft hyphens, or homoglyphs; also confirmed directly that the text contains no em dashes and no curly quotes.
